Ashu Sharma
--Applicant
 Versus
State Of Uttarakhand
--Respondent
Hon'ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
Mr. Pranav Singh, learned Counsel for the applicant.
2. Ms. Rangoli Purohit, learned AGA for the State.
3. Mr. Gaurav Singh, learned Counsel has instructions
to appear on behalf of the informant. He seeks and is
granted 24 hours' time to file power in the Registry.
4. The applicant has sought anticipatory bail in respect
of First Information Report No.0294 of 2026 dated
14.07.2026 registered with Police Station Bhagwanpur,
District Haridwar under Section 80(2) of BNS, 2023.
5. In the FIR, it was alleged by the informant that his
daughter was married with Shubham Sharma on
18.11.2024 as per Hindu rituals. Soon after the marriage,
the members of in-laws house began to harass and torture
the victim on the pretext of bringing lesser dowry, and a
demand of Rs.10.00 lakh besides some gold articles was
consistently being made. The FIR was lodged against
seven persons. On 13.07.2026, the daughter of informant
died and on 14.07.2026, informant was informed about the
occurrence.
6. The matter was investigated which resulted into
exoneration of other accused persons and submitting
charge-sheet against present applicant (Nanad) and

UKHC010198832026
2026:UHC:10522
husband of victim. Hence the applicant is before this Court
seeking anticipatory bail.
7. It is submitted on behalf of applicant that applicant is
a lady; she is residing in her matrimonial house situated at
Nazibabad (U.P.) along with her husband; she is the
mother of two children, one of which was recently born;
and applicant has no concern with the dowry demand.
8. On the other hand, learned Counsel appearing for the
State as also learned Counsel appearing for informant
vehemently opposed the anticipatory bail application; it
was argued that the applicant along with main accused
(husband) physically and mentally tortured the daughter of
informant and on non-fulfillment of demand, she was
coerced to commit suicide.
9. From the averments made in the body of FIR, it
appears that the applicant used to instigate her brother
(main accused) against the deceased by various kinds;
present applicant used to reproach the deceased for not
bringing gold ring, gold tops, and she also made a demand
of Rs.11,000/- which could be made available by the
mother of deceased.
10. This is a case where a young lady lost her life just
within 18 months of her marriage by committing suicide;
there are allegations of demand of dowry and harassment
against the applicant.
11. The Call Details Report (CDR) collected during
investigation also reflect that on the date of incident,
applicant was present in her matrimonial house located in

UKHC010198832026
2026:UHC:10522
Village Kunja Bahadarpur, Tehsil Roorkee, District
Haridwar. Further, the documents adduced by applicant
regarding the recent birth of her child also reflect that the
said child too was born in her matrimonial house.
12. Moreover, there is no possibility of present case being
a false one inasmuch as the FIR was lodged against seven
accused persons in which the applicant was also named
but the charge-sheet was filed only in respect of applicant
(Nanad) and her brother (husband).
13. Looking to the heinousness of offence coupled with
entire facts and circumstances of the case, the Court is of
the opinion that it is not a fit case to grant anticipatory bail
to the applicant at this stage.
14. Accordingly, the anticipatory bail application is
rejected.
15. However, the applicant would be at liberty to
surrender before the Court of competent jurisdiction within
15 days.
16. Pending application, if any, stands disposed of.
(Pankaj Purohit, J.)
 18.11.2026 R.Dang
